doctrine: OOZEMeter may say less, but it may not confidently say more than the evidence supports. Independence is never inferred from naming; it is proved by traversal over this graph.

readme.query: isUpstream(x, y) = there exists a directed path x -> … -> y in edges.
readme.independence: upstreamRawSeries(y) = { n : n.kind === "raw_series" and isUpstream(n, y) }. Two sensors are independent iff their upstreamRawSeries sets are disjoint.
readme.scoredEdges: Edges carrying scored:false reach a reader surface but not a stress value. Independence queries about SCORE must exclude them; queries about PUBLISHED CLAIMS must include them.
readme.aliasRule: Resolve every name through `aliases` to a node id BEFORE querying. Never compare names. `aliasCollisions` lists the tokens where name-based comparison gives the wrong answer.

assertions.why: Defect D1. scripts/collect.js:110 — housing = max(interp(mortgageRate, MORTGAGE30US), interp(mortgageDelinq, DRSFRMACBS)). Any cross-check pairing housing against foreclosures is circular.
The other end of D1. Both ends true ⇒ the pair shares a raw series ⇒ ILLEGAL cross-check.
INDPRO must NOT be upstream of jobs. jobs = max(UNRATE, ICSA-4wk) only. This is what makes jobs:manufacturing a legal pair.
Full disjointness both directions: {UNRATE, ICSA} ∩ {INDPRO, AMTMNO} = ∅.
The transitive deflator dependency. GASREGW is CPI-deflated AND rebased to the newest CPI print (scripts/collect.js:113).
gas and inflation both read CPIAUCNS. Pairing them in any cross-check, contrast or "these two disagree" claim would be D1 again.
Proves market.html:79 / market-pages.js:32: "they overlap in exactly one place". True at series identity. NOT a claim of economic orthogonality.
The name collision does NOT correspond to a shared series. Household credit reads DRCCLACBS; ward credit reads NFCI.

Backs "Ward M … does not affect the Ooze Score" (scripts/collect-market.js:138).
AMTMNO is display-only. It reaches the reader surface but not the stress value.
The largest-remainder split normalizes by wsum, so every weighted line is upstream of every OTHER line's ounce count. "Employment was N of the month's M ounces" is a claim about all seven lines.
The divergence series is not a comparison of two disjoint measurement systems.

crosscheckPolicy.rule: A cross-check between weighted line L and comparison sensor C is LEGAL only if (a) C carries zero score weight, (b) upstreamRawSeries(L) ∩ upstreamRawSeries(C) = ∅, and (c) delta(L) and delta(C) are computed over the SAME month pair.

failsConditionC.note: NO currently published pair satisfies condition (c). delta:household:manufacturing steps over INDPRO's own latest month pair; delta:household:foreclosures steps over a QUARTER; delta of every weighted line steps over the headline month pair M vs P.

hiddenCircularRelationships.title: Every weighted line is upstream of every other line's ounce count
paths: stress:household:<any weighted line> → derived:weighted-sum:household → contribution:household:<any other weighted line> (scripts/collect.js:127-135)
hiddenCircularRelationships.state: LIVE AND PUBLISHED. contribₖ = floor(ooze × wₖ·stressₖ / Σw·stress), then largest-remainder to foot exactly to the headline.
hiddenCircularRelationships.whyItMatters: The sentence 'employment was the largest source of financial pressure — 2 of the month's 26 ounces' (scripts/story.js:80) reads as a statement about employment. It is arithmetically a statement about all seven lines: if gas falls, employment's ounce count can rise without employment moving at all. Any cross-check, ranking claim, or 'largest pressure' claim built on contributions inherits every line's dependencies.
hiddenCircularRelationships.whatWouldRepublishIt: Already published. The exposure is a future cross-check or divergence claim keyed on contributions rather than stresses.

hiddenCircularRelationships.title: The divergence series is not a comparison of two disjoint instruments
hiddenCircularRelationships.state: LATENT DISCLOSURE GAP. data/market-history.json's note (scripts/build-market-divergence.js:47) discloses vintage basis and the breadth-transform mismatch, and says nothing about the shared series. market.html:79 discloses the overlap in the gauge paragraph, not beside the chart.
hiddenCircularRelationships.whyItMatters: A divergence of D between two instruments that share an input is not the same evidence as a divergence of D between two instruments that share nothing. The shared component is small (3% of one side, 16.7% of the other) but it is nonzero and it is exactly the component that moves in a funding crisis — the episodes the chart is used to narrate.

hiddenCircularRelationships.title: The revision log is partly self-generated: a new CPI print re-indexes the whole gas history, which the revision detector records as a change to published history
paths: raw:fred:CPIAUCNS → derived:latest-observation:CPIAUCNS → derived:real-price:GAS (every month) → score:household:history → artifact:revisions → claim:editorial:confidence
hiddenCircularRelationships.state: LIVE. scripts/integrity.js:50-54 already names the phenomenon ('the instrument re-indexing itself') and types the record honestly as 'history-changed-cause-unattributed'. The confidence sentence then counts those records and publishes 'N recorded changes to published history on the public record'.
hiddenCircularRelationships.whyItMatters: The count conflates two different events — an upstream source revising a past value, and OOZEMeter rescaling its own history because a new month of CPI arrived. The gate does not distinguish them; the prose does not either. A monthly deflator rebase can inflate a public integrity statistic.

currentlyUnverifiableRelationships.title: Flat-month semantics: forward-filled lines print "was flat this month" when the truth is "no new observation"
